page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.xlarge belongs to the ecs.g8a instance family and features a general-purpose hardware architecture. Built on x86_64 architecture, it is powered by a 2.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9T24 processor with 2 physical cores and 4 threads, providing 4 dedicated vCPUs. The instance includes 16 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4 GB per core. Cache configuration comprises 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16), AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. It does not include local NVMe storage, relying on attached network block storage, and operates with a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

In benchmark testing, the ecs.g8a.xlarge exhibits distinct performance patterns across workloads. Single-core processing is a key strength, achieving a top 25% performance result in stress-ng single-core tests. Multi-core performance in stress-ng falls within the average 50% range, reflecting its two-core physical topology. PassMark testing places its overall CPU, encryption, and memory bandwidth performance within average tiers. However, the server exhibits lower comparative throughput in specialized and IO-intensive areas, ranking in the lower 25% for PassMark extended instructions, database operations, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput.

The server provides a resource-dense configuration for single-threaded processing while maintaining a standard general-purpose memory allocation. Given the absence of bundled local NVMe storage and modest baseline network bandwidth, its resource profile balances steady compute capabilities against modest external IO limits. The instance is suited for general-purpose application hosting, microservices, backend control planes, and light web processing workloads that benefit from solid single-core performance without requiring heavy database IOPS or high multi-threaded output.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance based on the x86_64 architecture, powered by an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at 2.7 GHz. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores, coupled with 16 GB of memory for a standard 1:4 CPU-to-RAM allocation ratio. The hardware includes 32 MB L3 cache, support for AVX-512 extensions, and a 2 Gbps baseline network interface, while offering no local storage. Benchmark results show strong single-core CPU execution, ranking in the top tier for single-thread stress-ng tests, alongside middle-tier results in multi-core compute, encryption, and memory handling. Lower benchmark metrics in database operations, Redis throughput, and static web serving highlight trade-offs in heavy I/O environments. This instance is best suited for general-purpose applications, microservices, and single-thread intensive computing tasks.
